title: The Confirmation of Blood
summary: The rite that marks a Cainite as one of the Faithful.

claims.text: The rite mirrors the Catholic sacrament of confirmation: a priest anoints the subject with holy chrism on the brow and in the mouth and prays that the Holy Spirit dwell in that heart for ever.
The Faithful are very inward-looking, so this rite can decide whether a Cainite is believed to be a true fellow worshipper.
It and the road's other rites are usually held in a real place of worship, though confession can be heard anywhere, often in a Confessor's own rooms.

title: Synods of the Road of Heaven
summary: How the Faithful keep in touch across Christendom.

claims.text: Each year at the Feast of the Epiphany a synod's high priest receives word from the road's elders on the state and direction of the road.
The letter often carries a summons, and the synod must then send an envoy, usually the high priest, to a special gathering whose time and place only the recipient is told.

title: The Ashirra
summary: The Muslim Cainites of the Islamic world.

claims.text: The Ashirra keep a Hierarchy of Sins much like the Road of Heaven's, built on the precepts of Islam.
They forbid Embracing anyone without that person's consent; devout Ashirra can justify almost any Embrace, but the spirit of the rule is usually kept, and wilful breaches are punished.
They call the hidden agents of ruin the agh, the arrogant ones; these are the sect's greatest worry, and many Ashirra are wary to the point of paranoia.

title: The Diet of Jerusalem
summary: The truce that bound the Cainite princes of the Holy Land.

claims.text: This landmark accord gathered every ruling prince of the Holy Land, from as far as Cyprus and Tripoli, into a ten-year truce and pact of mutual aid.
It was the idea of the Salubri Qawiyya el-Ghaduba, the Lioness of Jerusalem, who called it after almost single-handedly destroying the Tremere of Jerusalem.

title: The Penitent Faithful
summary: Austere, mostly Low Clan Cainites devoted to atonement.

claims.text: While the High Clans fight over land and money, a small, mostly Low Clan faction holds that Cainites are damned by God and must atone.
Even among the Faithful they are austere: unlife should be neither pleasant nor safe, and their state is both a test and a last chance to prove themselves to their Creator.
Not every follower of the Via Caeli sees the curse as a curse; some read their power as proof of God's favour and come to think themselves above humanity.
